hero.lead: A nation of 10.8 million with a €21.9 billion recovery and resilience plan and two thirds of its power renewable.

capital.heading: Clean power and recovery, and a living income for all.

record.text: Recovery and resilience plan: €21.905 billion, the final revised allocation, completed by the tenth and last payment request of 29 September 2026
Investment mobilised in Portugal by the EIB Group in 2025, around 4% of GDP; more than €3 billion of housing finance committed across 2025 and 2026
Total direct debt of the State at 30 June 2026, from €315.2 billion at 31 December 2025
General government gross debt, share of GDP, 2025

register.name: New 20-year Treasury bond, OT 3.875% June 2046
register.detail: IGCP, the debt agency · syndicated 28 May 2026 · coupon 3.875% · matures 15 June 2046 · settled 4 June 2026
register.note: A new 20-year benchmark of the Republic, sold through a syndicate of banks
register.text: A new 20-year bond of the Portuguese Republic, sold by syndicate at a coupon of 3.875%. It funds the central government budget as a whole, which carries the seven standards; its proceeds are not earmarked to any one of them.

register.name: New 10-year Treasury bond, OT 3.25% June 2036
register.detail: IGCP, the debt agency · syndicated 8 January 2026 · coupon 3.25% · matures 13 June 2036
register.note: A new 10-year benchmark of the Republic, sold through a syndicate of banks
register.text: A new 10-year bond of the Portuguese Republic, sold by syndicate at a coupon of 3.25%. It funds the central government budget as a whole, which carries the seven standards; its proceeds are not earmarked to any one of them.

register.name: IFRRU 2030 rental housing line
register.detail: European Investment Bank · Signed 3 November 2026 · EIB release 4 November 2026 · Build-to-Rent and Renovate-to-Rent
register.note: More than 64% of the homes supported are expected to be in cohesion regions
register.text: Loans through participating financial intermediaries to build and renovate homes for rent at affordable or moderate prices, under the IFRRU 2030 financial instrument. It is aimed at the shelter standard.

register.name: Extreme weather recovery package
register.detail: European Investment Bank Group · Announced 27 October 2026 · Expected by the end of 2026
register.note: €250 million to the Republic; €500 million to Banco Português de Fomento
register.text: Financing for the Republic to rebuild municipal infrastructure damaged by extreme weather, and a loan to Banco Português de Fomento for reconstruction by small and mid-sized firms.

register.name: Recovery and resilience plan
register.detail: European Union · Final revised allocation · Tenth and last payment request submitted 29 September 2026
register.note: Tenth and last payment request: €4,672 million, net of advances
register.text: EU funding, in grants and loans, for agreed reforms and investments; all 379 milestones and targets reported as met.

register.name: Social housing framework loan
register.detail: European Investment Bank · First €500 million tranche signed 7 September 2026 · Local Housing Strategies
register.note: Supports the First Right programme of access to housing; total project cost about €4.36 billion
register.text: More than 50,000 new and rehabilitated homes across Portugal for vulnerable families, under the Local Housing Strategies of the municipalities. It is aimed at the shelter standard.

register.name: Affordable housing framework loan
register.detail: European Investment Bank · First €450 million tranche signed 18 September 2025
register.note: Implemented by IHRU, the housing institute, under the National Affordable Housing Programme
register.text: About 12,000 affordable rental homes across the country, let at rents below the market. It is aimed at the shelter standard.

register.name: InvestEU Fomento-FEI
register.detail: Government of Portugal · Announced 11 July 2025 · Largest InvestEU national compartment in Europe
register.note: Backed by €450 million of the recovery plan, a €50 million State guarantee and €490 million of EIF resources
register.text: Lending expected to be mobilised for more than 40,000 small firms, small mid-caps and individuals, through Banco Português de Fomento and the European Investment Fund. It is aimed at the livelihood standard.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Clean Grid
items.label: Of electricity from renewable sources, 2021
items.text: Power from water, wind and sun already flows; every new connection can be clean.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: Standing forest that stores carbon and water, and can earn as it stands.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 12.7% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: The Farmland
items.label: Of the land in agriculture, 2023
items.text: Land that can feed the nation and earn abroad, valued and financed against its harvest.

items.name: The Fresh Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water a person, 2022
items.text: Rain and rivers renewed every year: power, irrigation and drinking water.

items.name: Coopérnico
items.text: A non-profit cooperative electricity supplier with more than 6,950 members that offers 100% renewable electricity, had 49 solar plants of 2,932 kWp at the end of 2025 and helps citizens set up renewable energy communities.

items.name: Teach For Portugal
items.text: An association whose leadership development programme works to reduce educational inequality for children and young people from the most disadvantaged backgrounds, financed in the North from September 2025 to August 2027 by a €199,183 social impact bond whose private investors are repaid from EU funds for each person positively impacted, with similar bonds in the Centro, Alentejo and Algarve.

items.name: É um Restaurante, Associação CRESCER
items.text: Restaurants open to the public, run by Associação CRESCER since 2019, that create training and work for people who are or have been homeless; the sixth such project opened in the Parque Central of Amadora in April 2026.

coverage.gap_text: Of people in Portugal live below the national poverty line.

guarantees.name: Food
guarantees.note: Not food insecure; 11.9% are moderately or severely food insecure

guarantees.name: Shelter
guarantees.note: Safely managed sanitation; 0.1% of city dwellers live in slums

guarantees.name: Energy
guarantees.note: 99% cook with clean fuels and technology; 100% have electricity

guarantees.name: Education
guarantees.note: 92% of children read a simple text by the end of primary school

guarantees.name: Livelihoods
guarantees.note: Above the national poverty line; 16.4% live below it
